conflicts: Weight: the Baby Lock spec sheet says 16 lb and a non-maker Amazon listing snippet gave 7.8 kg (17.2 lb); 16 lb is used and it is unconfirmed whether either figure is a shipping weight.

Stitch width: the Baby Lock spec sheet gives one dial range of 1.5 to 7.5 mm, while our earlier spec from a non-maker listing split it into 5.5 to 7.5 mm (4 thread) and 3.0 to 7.5 mm (3 thread); the maker range is used and the thread-count split is unverified until the manual is read.

Differential feed: the Baby Lock spec sheet gives 2:1 for gathering and 3:4 (0.75) for stretching, while our earlier spec from a non-maker listing said 0.6 to 2.0; the 0.6 lower bound is not on the spec sheet, so maker wording is used.
Threads: the spec sheet lists 2 thread stitches (rolled hem and flatlock with 2 or 3 threads), which our earlier spec and FAQ omitted; coverstitch is not listed on the spec sheet.

Model revisions: the spec sheet is for the BLE1AT-2; the original BLE1AT is an older version, and PatternReview and Reddit sources mix BLE1AT, BLE1AT-2 and the Imagine Wave (BLE3ATW), so owner evidence below is not all BLE1AT-2.
Dimensions: the 13.4 x 11 x 11.4 in figure is from a non-maker listing; the Baby Lock spec sheet does not publish dimensions.

Price: Baby Lock publishes no price and no current new dealer price was found; owners on PatternReview reported paying $950 and $1,800 new in earlier years and one Reddit comment put the Imagine near $2,000, so the catalog shows [verify].
claims: "Jet-Air Threading" of the lower loopers by lever (Baby Lock marketing name, spec sheet and brochure)
"Automatic Thread Delivery" and "no tension adjustments" (Baby Lock marketing, spec sheet and brochure)
"Baby Lock's most popular serger" (Baby Lock marketing, not verified by us)
"Can you imagine how easy serging would be if you didn't have to thread the loopers" (Baby Lock brochure headline)

editorial.verdict: A discontinued Baby Lock 4/3/2 thread serger whose Jet-Air threading and Automatic Thread Delivery are maker claims that owners mostly, not always, bear out.
editorial.whoFor: A sewist who wants air threading and no tension dials, is buying used or from a dealer's remaining stock, and can live without a published coverstitch.
editorial.skipIf: You want a current model with a fresh warranty, need coverstitch, or can buy a new air-threading Juki online instead.
editorial.keySpec: 4/3/2 thread · 1,500 spm · 1.5 to 7.5 mm width · 2:1 and 3:4 differential · 16 lb
strengths: The maker lists 4, 3 and 2 thread serging with rolled hem and flatlock, so it covers more than the 3/4 thread machines it is often grouped with
Owners report threading as easy and the machine as reliable, with some units still in use after six years or more, though the evidence mixes BLE1AT, BLE1AT-2 and older units
Baby Lock states a 25 year limited warranty with 10 year parts, 5 year electrical and 1 year labor on its spec sheet
weaknesses: Discontinued: Baby Lock lists the Imagine under previous models, and a PatternReview thread says the Victory replaced it
Owners report tension trouble on stretchy or mismatched fabrics, and some find manual tensioning is still the real annoyance; the maker's no-tension wording is a claim
Some owners report air-threader and looper-thread problems (a broken lower thread, an unthreaded looper, thread cone fit), and one reports worn tension springs with a costly repair

checks.title: Confirm BLE1AT-2, not BLE1AT or Imagine Wave
checks.body: The spec sheet here is for the BLE1AT-2. The original BLE1AT is an older version and the Wave (BLE3ATW) is a separate wave stitch model, and used listings and reviews mix them. One Reddit buyer of a used BLE1AT-1 reported a dead air threader.

checks.title: Ask what the warranty covers on a used unit
checks.body: The 25 year limited, 10 year parts, 5 year electrical and 1 year labor terms come from the spec sheet; the warranty PDF was not fetched. On a used or demo unit ask the dealer what coverage remains.

checks.title: Price the Victory and the Juki MO-1000 first
checks.body: A PatternReview thread says the Victory replaced the Imagine, and Juki's MO-1000 is the air-threading serger sold online. Baby Lock publishes no price, so get dealer quotes before paying near new money for a used Imagine.

realCost: Serger thread: owners report taller cones can cause feed problems and Maxi-Loc cones worked better for one
Household needles in HAx1SP, 130/705H or ELx705CF per the spec sheet
Serger oil and a lint brush; owners mention an occasional service
Tension spring service out of warranty, reported by one PatternReview owner as not cheap

faqs.q: Is the Baby Lock Imagine discontinued?
faqs.a: Yes. Baby Lock lists the Imagine under previous model accessories, and a PatternReview thread on the new lineup says the Victory replaced it, though dealer pages still show Imagine listings.
A PatternReview thread says the Victory replaced it. One Reddit commenter put the Imagine near $2,000 and the Victory near $3,500; Baby Lock publishes dealer pricing only, so treat that as a belief.

faqs.q: How much does the Imagine cost?
faqs.a: Baby Lock does not publish prices and no current new price was found, so it shows [verify]. Owners reported paying $950 and $1,800 new in earlier years, and a used unit sold on eBay near $550.

faqs.q: Does the Imagine have tension dials?
faqs.a: Baby Lock markets Automatic Thread Delivery and no tension adjustments, which are its claims. Owner reports are mixed: some report no tension issues in about six years, others report tension trouble on stretchy fabrics.
The Baby Lock BLE1AT-2 spec sheet gives 1,500 stitches per minute.

faqs.q: Does the Imagine do 2 thread stitches or coverstitch?
faqs.a: The spec sheet lists 4, 3 and 2 thread serging, with rolled hem and flatlock using 2 or 3 threads. It does not list coverstitch.

faqs.q: What is the difference between BLE1AT and BLE1AT-2?
faqs.a: The BLE1AT is the older version and the BLE1AT-2 the later one. A PatternReview thread describes the difference as minor, but our spec sheet is for the BLE1AT-2 only and we did not compare the two documents.
The Baby Lock spec sheet says 16 lb. An Amazon listing snippet gave 7.8 kg (17.2 lb); the maker figure is used here.

faqs.q: What needles does the Imagine take?
faqs.a: The Baby Lock spec sheet lists the household needle system HAx1SP, 130/705H and ELx705CF. The manual was not fetched.
The spec sheet states 25 years limited, 10 years parts, 5 years electrical and 1 year labor. The warranty PDF was not fetched, so check transfer terms with the dealer.

faqs.q: Is the Imagine the same as the Imagine Wave?
faqs.a: No. The Imagine Wave (BLE3ATW) is a separate wave stitch model, and its reviews are mixed in with the Imagine on PatternReview.
